greeting: Ataniup Aqqutaanik, Ilitsinik, Irniup, ammalu Anirniup Sarumajup. Ataniq ilitsinniittuq.
penitential: Ataniq, ungasiktumik asanninirnik takujauvut. Ataniq, tusaguk. Ataniq, tusaguk.
psalm_response: I shall live in the house of the Lord all the days of my life.
homily:
Imagine, if you will, the hum of a busy airport terminal. The departure boards are flickering with names of cities—Tokyo, Beijing, Rome. There is a specific, electric energy in that space, a sense that we are all waiting for something grand to happen. For Benjamin, this was not just a place to travel; it was a sanctuary of wonder. He would stand there, perhaps with his father, eyes tracking the graceful arc of a Boeing 737 as it lifted into the sky, his heart soaring along with it. He had this beautiful, quiet dream of 'con chim airlines'—a project born of his own brilliant mind and his joy in the mechanics of flight. When he spoke of it, he would giggle, a light, infectious sound that seemed to hold the very promise of the future. That giggle was the sound of a boy who knew, even then, that the world was vast and that he was invited to be part of its movement.

Today, the Prophet Isaiah speaks to us of a different kind of gathering, a far greater destination. He says, 'On this mountain the LORD of hosts will provide for all peoples a feast of rich food and choice wines.' This is the image that must run through our hearts today: the Banquet. We are not meant for the small, cramped rooms of our own sorrow or the quiet, empty spaces of our grief. We are invited to a mountain, to a table that never ends. Isaiah tells us that on this mountain, God will 'destroy the veil that veils all peoples, the web that is woven over all nations; he will destroy death forever.'

I want to speak to you, Alan, Thao, and Ryan, with the utmost honesty. I know the veil feels heavy. I know there are mornings when you wake up and the silence of the house is not a peace, but an ache. You look for Ben in the rhythm of the morning, in the way the light hits the kitchen table, in the quiet corners of your heart. That ache is not a sign that you have failed or that you have forgotten; it is a sign of how deeply you loved, and how deeply you were loved in return. But look at the promise: 'The Lord GOD will wipe away the tears from every face.' This is not a future promise only; it is a present reality. He is wiping them away even now, through the grace that sustains you when you feel you cannot take another step.

Then, the Gospel breaks into this space with a startling, almost jarring invitation. A king throws a wedding feast for his son, but the invited guests make excuses. They have farms to tend, business to conduct. They are distracted by the 'now.' And so, the king sends his servants out to the main roads to gather everyone—the bad and the good alike. The hall is filled. It is a reminder that the invitation to heaven is not earned by perfection or status; it is a free gift given to those who are found on the road of life.

There is a man in the parable who is cast out for not wearing a wedding garment. It can seem harsh to our ears. But think of the garment not as a costume, but as the heart itself. To be dressed for the feast is to be clothed in the grace that God has poured into us. Benjamin, our dear Ben, was a boy who understood this grace. He lived with a curiosity that was, in itself, a form of prayer. Whether he was coding games in his GitHub repository, or reaching out with a heart so tender that he wanted to give his own savings to help his uncle, he was putting on the 'garment' of love. He didn't just study the world; he sought to serve it. He was a boy who looked at the horizon and saw not just distance, but possibility.

I want to speak to the guilt that sometimes hides in the corners of a parent's heart. There are times when we look back and wonder if we missed a sign, if we could have done more, if we could have changed the outcome. Let me say this as clearly as I can: neither you nor your son failed. God does not deal in the ledger of human blame. Illness is not a punishment, and it is not a reflection of your care. You loved him with a devotion that is holy. You held him, you traveled with him, you listened to his stories about airplanes until you knew the wingspan of every jet in the sky. That was not just parenting; that was participating in God's own love. You are absolved of the weight of 'what if.' You did everything a human heart could do, and God, who is the source of all love, holds both you and Ben in a grace that is beyond any human error.

Ryan, my brother, you know this better than anyone. You lived the adventure with him. You saw the smile, you shared the jokes, you stood together in front of the cockpit displays. When you feel that the world is too quiet, remember that the bond you have with Ben is not broken by the veil of death. It is simply hidden for a while. You carry his spirit in your own, in the way you approach your studies, in the way you carry your own curiosity into the future. Live for him, yes, but live for yourself, too—full of the same joy that made him giggle at the thought of his own airline. He is cheering for you from the best seat in the house.

We are all invited to this feast. We are all, at times, the ones wandering the main roads, feeling lost or tired. But the King is looking for us. He is finding us exactly where we are—in our grief, in our confusion, in our quiet moments of prayer. He wants us at the table. He wants us to taste the 'rich food' of His presence. The 'wedding garment' is simply our willingness to let Him love us, even when we feel we have nothing left to offer.

So, what can you carry out the door today? It is a small thing, but it is enough. The next time you look at the sky and see a plane, or the next time you feel a sudden, sharp pang of missing him, do not let it lead you into the dark. Let it be a reminder of the 'con chim airlines' of his heart—a reminder that he is soaring, that he is free, and that he is waiting for you at the table on the mountain. Take a deep breath, and whisper a 'Good morning' to him, just as he always did for his father. He is listening. He is home. And one day, the feast will be complete for all of us. Until then, walk in the light, and know that you are never, ever walking alone.
spiritual_communion: My Jesus, I believe that You are present in the Most Holy Sacrament. I love You above all things, and I desire to receive You into my soul. Since I cannot at this moment receive You sacramentally, come at least spiritually into my heart. I embrace You as if You were already there and unite myself wholly to You. Never permit me to be separated from You. Amen.
closing: May the Lord of the feast bless you and keep you, and may His face shine upon you forever. Amen.
standing_petitions: Benjamin Vo ammalu tamaita tuqusimajut, Ataniup qaumaniangani inuuliritsi.
Tamaita uqumaittumik atuqtut, Ataniq ikajullugu niriunnik ammalu asanninirmik.

readings.label: Atuagak 1
readings.text: On this mountain the LORD of hosts will provide for all peoples a feast of rich food and choice wines, juicy, rich food and pure, choice wines. On this mountain he will destroy the veil that veils all peoples, the web that is woven over all nations; he will destroy death forever. The Lord GOD will wipe away the tears from every face; the reproach of his people he will remove from the whole earth; for the LORD has spoken. On that day it will be said: "Behold our God, to whom we looked to save us! This is the LORD for whom we looked; let us rejoice and be glad that he has saved us!" For the hand of the LORD will rest on this mountain.

readings.label: Atuagak 2
readings.text: Brothers and sisters: I know how to live in humble circumstances; I know also how to live with abundance. In every circumstance and in all things I have learned the secret of being well fed and of going hungry, of living in abundance and of being in need. I can do all things in him who strengthens me. Still, it was kind of you to share in my distress. My God will fully supply whatever you need, in accord with his glorious riches in Christ Jesus. To our God and Father, glory forever and ever. Amen.

readings.label: Gospel
readings.text: Jesus again in reply spoke to the chief priests and elders of the people in parables, saying, "The kingdom of heaven may be likened to a king who gave a wedding feast for his son. He dispatched his servants to summon the invited guests to the feast, but they refused to come. A second time he sent other servants, saying, 'Tell those invited: "Behold, I have prepared my banquet, my calves and fattened cattle are killed, and everything is ready; come to the feast."' Some ignored the invitation and went away, one to his farm, another to his business. The rest laid hold of his servants, mistreated them, and killed them. The king was enraged and sent his troops, destroyed those murderers, and burned their city. Then he said to his servants, 'The feast is ready, but those who were invited were not worthy to come. Go out, therefore, into the main roads and invite to the feast whomever you find.' The servants went out into the streets and gathered all they found, bad and good alike, and the hall was filled with guests. But when the king came in to meet the guests, he saw a man there not dressed in a wedding garment. The king said to him, 'My friend, how is it that you came in here without a wedding garment?' But he was reduced to silence. Then the king said to his attendants, 'Bind his hands and feet, and cast him into the darkness outside, where there will be wailing and grinding of teeth.' Many are invited, but few are chosen."

pet_prayers.text: Ben ơi, trong giấc ngủ anh Huy đã thấy Ben về thăm anh, trao cho anh lời cầu nguyện để hai anh em mình lại được tìm thấy nhau. Xin Chúa thương nhậm lời Ben, cho Ben được hưởng ngàn thu bình an bên Chúa. Nếu có thể, xin Ben lại ghé thăm anh trong những giấc mơ tiếp theo nhé, dù chỉ là một lời chào hay một nụ cười thân thương như ngày nào.

pet_prayers.name: Dad
pet_prayers.text: Ben, my sweet boy, I miss you so much. Thank you for visiting me and Chú Chris last night. He told me he saw you flying a helicopter—so free, joyful, and strong up there. Down here, Mom and I are crying more and more each day. A piece of my heart feels completely dead without you, Ben. Please watch over us, pray for your mom, your brother Ryan, and me, and give us the strength to keep going. We love you forever

pet_prayers.name: Dad
pet_prayers.text: Today marks 100 days without you. Miss you a whole a lot Ben. Feel free to visit any time! See you around buddy! Love you!

Ben ơi, nay anh M đi xử lý hồ sơ ở Cam Ranh, đi ngang qua Cam Ranh Airport. Rồi cuộc nói chuyện về máy bay của Ben lại ùa về, nhớ nhiều kỷ niệm về Ben lắm ( anh M sẽ giữ kín kakaka). Quỷ nhỏ, tự nhiên nghĩ về mày buồn dễ sợ. Hãy đi đến những nơi mà Ben muốn nha và đừng quên là luôn nhớ về gia đình mình nhé, thương em trai nhiều. Giá như !!!!!!!!!

pet_prayers.name: Dad
pet_prayers.text: What happened my son? It's been 3 months since you left us. Missing you so much my whole body aches. Mom cries every day now... What are we going to do now Ben?  Please pray for us.

pet_prayers.name: Dad
pet_prayers.text:
Hey Ben,

Rafael Rizzo and his little brother Ben really need your help right now. Please bless them with good health and give them the strength to get through this together. Please watch over Brandon and Flor's health, too.

I miss you a whole bunch. I know you're up in heaven watching over all of us. Whenever you're able to, stop by to visit, yeah? I love you and miss you so much!

pet_prayers.name: Dad
pet_prayers.text:
Hey Ben - Miss you a whole bunch. Crying all day yesterday, i hope today will be better. Please guide our family through this grief... There's a 14 year old boy that just left earth on August 12... His name is Phero Aden Vo - look for him, maybe you guys can be friends...

Please pray for me and mom to have good health and strength.

I love and miss you Ben
